full_text_en:
Kunming Weihengli Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd. v. Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, Third Party: Donghua Subdistrict Office of Panlong District People's Government, Kunming — Administrative Penalty Dispute

Ruling Summary

1. According to Article 32 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the PRC, before making a decision on administrative penalty, an administrative organ shall inform the party of the facts, reasons, and basis for the administrative penalty decision, and shall inform the party of the rights he/she enjoys according to law. If an administrative organ fails to perform its obligation of notification in accordance with the above provisions, the administrative penalty procedure will be illegal.

2. Article 40 of the Urban Planning Law of the PRC provides: "Within a planned urban area, if a construction is carried out without a construction project planning permit or in violation of the provisions of a construction project planning permit, and seriously affects urban planning, the competent department of urban planning administration of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order the cessation of construction, and order demolition within a time limit or confiscate the illegal buildings, structures, or other facilities; if it affects urban planning but remedial measures may still be taken, the competent department of urban planning administration of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order correction within a time limit, and impose a fine." The subject of penalty under the above provision is the builder who carries out construction without a construction project planning permit or in violation of the provisions of a construction project planning permit, and an order for demolition within a time limit may only be made when the illegal construction reaches the extent of "seriously affecting urban planning".

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Xing Zhong Zi No. 1

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Kunming Weihengli Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 204-206 Xichang Road, Kunming.

Legal Representative: Chen Meili, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ma Huaide, lawyer of Beijing Jietong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Mengxin, lawyer of Beijing Shanggong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, domiciled at No. 118 Tuodong Road, Kunming.

Legal Representative: Zhou Fengyue, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Xiong Bin, lawyer of Yunnan Liu Hule Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Jin Xi, lawyer of Yunnan Liu Hule Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Donghua Subdistrict Office of Panlong District People's Government, Kunming, domiciled at No. 19 Bailong Road, Kunming.

Legal Representative: Hua Pirui, Director of the Subdistrict Office.

Agent ad litem: Chen Lei, lawyer of Jianwei (Kunming) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yuan Zhongbin, lawyer of Jianwei (Kunming) Law Firm.

Kunming Weihengli Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kunming Weihengli Company), appellant, appealed to this Court against the Administrative Judgment (2007) Yun Gao Xing Chu Zi No. 2 rendered by the Yunnan High People's Court, regarding its lawsuit against the illegal construction administrative penalty decision dated October 12, 2006, by Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning (Kun Planning Law Penalty (2006) No. 0063). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel with Li Guangyu presiding as the presiding judge, trial judge Qi Shukui, and acting trial judge Wang Da to hear the case. Clerk Li Lintao served as recorder. This case is now concluded.

Based on the evidence submitted by the parties and after court investigation and cross-examination, the Yunnan High People's Court found the following facts: On October 12, 2006, the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, based on the "12345" Mayor's Hotline Receipt and Assignment Form of the Kunming Municipal Government and the Letter of Transfer for Petition Matters from the Kunming Municipal Committee of the CPC and the Kunming Municipal People's Government, and after on-site survey and mapping, determined that the six-story comprehensive building (one underground floor, floor area 2,469.28 square meters; five above-ground floors, floor area 12,484.16 square meters) with a total floor area of 14,953.44 square meters constructed by the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office of Panlong District People's Government, Kunming (hereinafter referred to as Donghua Subdistrict Office), at Xiaolong Road, had not been approved by the competent department of urban planning administration, violating Article 32 of the Urban Planning Law of the PRC and Article 27 of the Yunnan Province Urban Planning Management Regulations, and constituted illegal construction. Therefore, pursuant to Article 40 of the Urban Planning Law of the PRC and Article 41 of the Yunnan Province Urban Planning Management Regulations, it made the administrative penalty decision for illegal construction (Kun Planning Law Penalty (2006) No. 0063), ordering the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, to demolish the illegally constructed comprehensive building project by itself before October 31, 2006. The plaintiff, Kunming Weihengli Company, was dissatisfied and filed an administrative lawsuit with the court on the grounds that the Xiaolong Road comprehensive building was built with its own investment, and the penalty decision of the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, had unclear facts, illegal procedures, and ultra vires administrative actions, infringing upon its lawful rights and interests. It requested the court to revoke the "Decision on Administrative Penalty for Illegal Construction" (Kun Planning Law Penalty (2006) No. 0063) of the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, to order the change of the penalty measure to a fine and handling of formalities, and to order the defendant to bear all litigation costs. During the litigation, the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, revoked the specific administrative act in question by its "Decision on Revoking the 'Decision on Administrative Penalty for Illegal Construction' (Kun Planning Law Penalty (2006) No. 0063)" (Suigui (2007) No. 217) on October 11, 2007.

The Yunnan High People's Court held upon trial: According to Article 32 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the PRC, before making an administrative penalty decision, an administrative organ shall inform the party of the facts, reasons, and basis for the administrative penalty decision, and shall inform the party of the rights he/she enjoys according to law. Before making the penalty decision (Kun Planning Law Penalty (2006) No. 0063), the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, did not inform the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, of the facts, reasons, and basis for the penalty decision and the rights the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, enjoyed according to law, and thus the procedure was illegal. According to Article 40 of the Urban Planning Law of the PRC, which provides: "Within a planned urban area, if a construction is carried out without a construction project planning permit or in violation of the provisions of a construction project planning permit, and seriously affects urban planning, the competent department of urban planning administration of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order the cessation of construction, and order demolition within a time limit or confiscate the illegal buildings, structures, or other facilities; if it affects urban planning but remedial measures may still be taken, the competent department of urban planning administration of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order correction within a time limit, and impose a fine." The subject of penalty for carrying out construction without a construction project planning permit or in violation of the provisions of a construction project planning permit is the builder of the illegal construction, and an order for demolition within a time limit may only be made when the illegal construction reaches the extent of "seriously affecting urban planning". The evidence provided by the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, was insufficient to prove that the builder of the Xiaolong Road comprehensive building was the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, and that the construction of the Xiaolong Road comprehensive building had reached the extent of "seriously affecting urban planning". Thus, the main evidence for the specific administrative act in question was insufficient. The specific administrative act in question in this case had insufficient evidence and illegal procedure, and should be revoked. However, during the litigation, the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, had already made a revocation decision. Pursuant to Article 50, paragraph 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, which provides: "If the defendant changes the original specific administrative act and the plaintiff does not withdraw the lawsuit, the people's court shall, upon trial finding the original specific administrative act unlawful, render a judgment confirming its illegality; if it finds the original specific administrative act lawful, it shall render a judgment rejecting the plaintiff's claims." Therefore, the people's court shall render a judgment confirming its illegality. Since the specific administrative act in question had been revoked by the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, on its own initiative during the litigation, the claim of the plaintiff, Kunming Weihengli Company, that "the penalty measure of Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning be changed to a fine and handling of formalities" could not be established. The court rendered a judgment confirming the illegality of the "Decision on Administrative Penalty for Illegal Construction" (Kun Planning Law Penalty (2006) No. 0063) made by the defendant, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, on October 12, 2006. It rejected the claim of the plaintiff, Kunming Weihengli Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd., that the penalty measure of Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning be changed to a fine and handling of formalities.

Kunming Weihengli Company was dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and appealed to this Court, arguing: The project in question is a government project and a government-invited investment project, and did not reach the extent of "seriously affecting urban planning" that would require demolition. The specific administrative act in question was obviously unfair. The first-instance judgment merely confirming the illegality of the administrative penalty decision in question was insufficient. The penalty decision, which was obviously unfair, should be changed from the perspective of protecting the parties' reliance interests. It requested the revocation of the second judgment of the first instance, and an order that Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning change its penalty decision to a fine and handling of formalities.

The respondent, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, argued in defense: The construction project in this case was an illegal building that had not undergone planning approval. The first-instance court confirmed the illegality of the specific administrative act that had been revoked, and rejected the appellee's request to change the penalty measure, which was correct in the application of law. It requested the second-instance court to uphold the first-instance judgment.

The third party at first instance, Donghua Subdistrict Office of Panlong District People's Government, Kunming, stated: It had no objection to the appeal request of Kunming Weihengli Company, but its statement that the project in question was a comprehensive renovation, improvement, and resettlement project led by the Panlong District Government did not conform to the objective facts of this case.

The relevant evidence provided by the parties to the first-instance court mainly included: the Mayor's Hotline Receipt and Assignment Form of Kunming Municipal Government, the "Urgent Report" of the staff of Yunnan Provincial Building Materials Company, the Letter of Transfer for Petition Matters, the "Organization Code Certificate" of the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, the "Power of Attorney" issued by the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, and the identity card of Dong Shiquan, the general layout plan and survey map, the "Decision on Administrative Penalty for Illegal Construction", the "Notice of Acceptance of Planning Inspection", the "Notice of Cessation of Work for Illegal Construction (Illegal Building) in Kunming (Stub)" and the "Service Receipt", the "Report on Coordinating and Resolving Issues Concerning the 'Xiaolong Sifangjie Flower and Bird Market'", and the "Decision of Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning on Revoking the 'Decision on Administrative Penalty for Illegal Construction' (Kun Planning Law Penalty (2006) No. 0063)".

The above evidence has been transferred to this Court together with the case files. Upon examination, it can be used as the basis for finding the facts of this case. The facts found by this Court based on the above evidence are no different from those in the original judgment.

This Court holds: According to Article 32 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the PRC, before making an administrative penalty decision, an administrative organ shall inform the party of the facts, reasons, and basis for the administrative penalty decision, and shall inform the party of the rights he/she enjoys according to law. Before making the administrative penalty decision (Kun Planning Law Penalty (2006) No. 0063), the respondent, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, did not inform the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, of the facts, reasons, and basis for the penalty decision and the rights the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, enjoyed according to law. The first-instance judgment's finding of procedural illegality was not erroneous.

Article 40 of the Urban Planning Law of the PRC provides: "Within a planned urban area, if a construction is carried out without a construction project planning permit or in violation of the provisions of a construction project planning permit, and seriously affects urban planning, the competent department of urban planning administration of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order the cessation of construction, and order demolition within a time limit or confiscate the illegal buildings, structures, or other facilities; if it affects urban planning but remedial measures may still be taken, the competent department of urban planning administration of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order correction within a time limit, and impose a fine." Accordingly, the subject of penalty for carrying out construction without a construction project planning permit or in violation of the provisions of a construction project planning permit is the builder of the illegal construction, and an order for demolition within a time limit may only be made when the illegal construction reaches the extent of "seriously affecting urban planning". The evidence provided by the respondent, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning, was insufficient to prove that the builder of the Xiaolong Road comprehensive building was the third party, Donghua Subdistrict Office, and that the construction of the Xiaolong Road comprehensive building had reached the extent of "seriously affecting urban planning". The first-instance judgment's finding that the main evidence for the specific administrative act in question was insufficient had factual and legal basis.

During the first-instance proceedings, Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning made a decision to revoke the original specific administrative act. Kunming Weihengli Company did not withdraw the lawsuit. The Yunnan High People's Court rendered a judgment confirming the illegality of the specific administrative act in question, which complied with the provisions of Article 50, paragraph 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. The appellant, Kunming Weihengli Company, requested an order that Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning change its penalty decision to a fine and handling of formalities. Since the specific administrative act in question had been revoked by Kunming Municipal Bureau of Planning on its own initiative during the litigation, the first-instance judgment's rejection of this claim was not improper. The appellant's grounds for appeal could not be established.

In conclusion, the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, correct application of laws and regulations, and lawful trial procedure. Pursuant to Article 61, item (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal rejected, the original judgment affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 50 shall be borne by the appellant, Kunming Weihengli Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Li Guangyu
Trial Judge: Qi Shukui
Acting Trial Judge: Wang Da

January 13, 2009

Clerk: Li Lintao
